Four call sites in the three modules call the single-argument `getGlobalProperty` and fall back silently when the value is missing. Best match first:

1. **idgen**, `IdgenEditPatientIdentifiersController.getImportantTypes()` (line 110). A null value is skipped by `StringUtils.isNotEmpty`, so the method silently returns an empty map.
2. **metadataexport**, `MetadataExportActivator.started()` (lines 40–41). `BooleanUtils.toBoolean(null)` is false, so export-on-startup is silently disabled.
3. **event**, `EventEngine.getExternalUrl()` (lines 194–207) and its caller `initializeIfNeeded()` (line 169). A null or empty `activeMQ.externalUrl` falls back to an embedded `vm://localhost` broker. The method only catches `NullPointerException`, so a new exception from the getter would escape it.
4. **idgen**, `LocationBasedSuffixProvider.getSuffixLocationAttributeType()` (lines 58–64). It caches the value, and a null value makes `equalsIgnoreCase(null)` false at line 43, so the lookup silently moves up the location tree.
5. **idgen**, `LocationBasedPrefixProvider.getPrefixLocationAttributeType()` (lines 58–64). This is the same pattern as item 4, using the prefix property and the usage at line 43.

Test stubs in idgen (`SequentialIdentifierGeneratorTest`, `LocationBasedPrefixProviderTest`) also call the one-argument form, but they mock it and don't depend on a default, so I left them out.

Coverage: I searched all three repositories for single-line calls. I checked for calls split across lines only in `openmrs-module-event`, where there were none. I did not run that check in metadataexport or idgen. I also did not read the usage context around line 43 in the two idgen providers; that line is cited from the search result.
